Tesla is winding down Cybertruck production next year to prioritize self-driving Cybercabs, amid struggles with mass-market sales, quality issues, and recalls [3, 4, 7].

* **Cybertruck Phase-Out:** CEO Elon Musk announced that Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas factory around the middle of next year to ramp up Cybercab robotaxis [3, 7, 8]. The vehicle struggled with poor sales in few markets, a polarizing design, quality-control issues, and voluntary recalls [1, 2, 3].
* **International Cancellations & Drops:** In late October 2026, Tesla canceled the Cybertruck in Australia and New Zealand after seven years of taking deposits [12].
* **Financial and Market Pressures:** Tesla reported a 43% drop in profits for the third quarter of 2026 [13], and Tesla and SpaceX experienced a combined market cap loss of over $420 billion over a two-day span in November [6].
* **Roadster Uncertainty:** Tesla stated it "cannot guarantee" that Roadster reservation holders will ever receive a car [14], following the vehicle's mid-October debut showcasing SpaceX thrusters [18].
* **Regulatory & Safety Scrutiny:** An NHTSA petition alleged in October that Tesla's robotaxis blow through school zones [19], and a Tesla Semi caught fire on Interstate 880 in late October [11].
* **Feature Rebranding:** In Europe, Tesla rebranded its "Full Self-Driving" software to "Tesla Assisted Driving" in October [20].
